findings.claim: Docstring calls the Arrhenius AF formula 'symmetric', but swapping use and stress temperatures gives the reciprocal (1/AF), not the same value — the exponent is antisymmetric, not symmetric.
findings.evidence: arrhenius_acceleration(25, 85, 0.7) * arrhenius_acceleration(85, 25, 0.7) == 1.0 exactly (numerically verified); AF(a,b) = exp(Ea/k(1/Ta - 1/Tb)) = 1/AF(b,a). A reader taking 'symmetric' literally (AF(a,b) == AF(b,a)) would invert an acceleration factor. The formula itself and all computed values are correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'swapping the two temperatures gives the reciprocal factor (AF -> 1/AF)' or 'the formula is antisymmetric in 1/T'.

result.checks_run: Re-derived and numerically reproduced every formula: (1) Arrhenius 52.8 anchor — exponent (0.97/8.617333262e-5)*(1/298.15 - 1/333.15) = 3.96636, AF = 52.792, matches doc and test within stated 1% tolerance; direction verified (AF>1 for stress>use, life_use = AF*life_stress, matching JESD91 semantics); Boltzmann eV/K constant matches CODATA via scipy.constants to 1.5e-15. (2) FIT = 1e9/MTTF and series-sum n*FIT — correct exponential-regime algebra; module MTTF = device MTTF/n verified. (3) survival_probability exp(-FIT*t*1e-9) — 1000 FIT for 1e6 h gives exp(-1), verified. (4) wearout_fraction lognormal CDF Phi(ln(t/t50)/sigma) via erf — cross-checked against scipy.stats.lognorm.cdf at 5 points spanning z from -15 to +10, agreement to <=3e-17; exact 0.5 at t50; tails clamp cleanly to 0.0/1.0 at t=1e-300 and 1e300; log-time symmetry F(t50/r)+F(t50*r)=1 holds. (5) Competing risks and module_survival — independently recomputed S = [exp(-fit*t*1e-9)*lognorm.sf(t)]^n with scipy for n=64: 0.27357935165362707, module returns identical value; XOR guard on (t50, sigma) verified. (6) wpe_derated — analytic values (0.20*(1-0.01*20)=0.16, 0.24 below ref), cap at 1.0, raise at <=0 verified; edge float case 0.01*(145-45) rounds to exactly 1.0 so the zero-derating test is deterministic under IEEE754. (7) Celsius->kelvin uses 273.15 with absolute-zero guard on all temperature inputs including wpe_derated's. (8) Convention check vs package: montecarlo.py converts metric ValueError to NaN corners, so ValueError-on-invalid here is the package-consistent choice; Laser(wpe in (0,1]) handoff verified against link.py:102. Ran full test suite: 33/33 pass. No wrong numbers found in any plausible use.

findings.claim: stacklevel=3 is hardcoded for the direct neff() call path, so when the warning is reached via group_index() or dispersion_ps_nm_km() it is attributed to waveguide.py internals (lines 214-216) instead of the user's call site.
findings.evidence: Numerically reproduced: Waveguide(width_um=0.033, height_um=0.22).group_index(1.55, 'TE') from a /tmp script emits three EimAccuracyWarning records attributed to src/siphon/waveguide.py lines 214/215/216 (the internal self.neff calls), not the caller's file, whereas a direct wg.neff() call is correctly attributed to the caller. Warning still fires and displays; only the reported location (and any location-based warning filters) is affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Not required for correctness. If desired, thread a stacklevel offset through neff/_neff_cached or bump stacklevel by 1 in group_index/dispersion callers; alternatively document that dispersion helpers attribute the warning to library code.

findings.claim: Docstring says the per-ring cost model 'match[es] :func:`tuning_power_mw`', but the two functions charge different powers for the same physical blue-shift situation: optimize_ring_assignment (correctly) charges the long way around, (FSR - |d|)/eff, while tuning_power_mw's existing contract charges |d|/eff for a blue-shift request (its own docstring claims the long way costs 'the same |detune|', which is physically wrong unless |d| = FSR/2). A user reproducing per-ring powers via tuning_power_mw(target - as_built) gets numbers that disagree with the optimizer by up to (FSR-|d|)/|d|.
findings.evidence: wdm.optimize_ring_assignment([1.0], fsr_nm=10.0, efficiency_nm_per_mw=1.0).per_ring_mw == (9.0,) (as-built +1 nm red of target, heater must go forward 9 nm to the next order — correct), but wdm.tuning_power_mw(-1.0, 1.0) == 1.0 mW for the identical physical blue-shift request: a 9x discrepancy. The new code itself is self-consistent and physically right; the misleading part is the 'matching tuning_power_mw' cross-reference plus the pre-existing (unchanged) tuning_power_mw docstring claim that the long way costs the same |detune|.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the cross-reference to the linear P = shift/efficiency model only, e.g. 'linear heater model P = shift/efficiency as in tuning_power_mw, but blue-shift requests are charged the full wrap cost (FSR - |d|), unlike tuning_power_mw which uses |d|'; optionally fix tuning_power_mw's docstring in a separate change.

result.checks_run: Re-derived h_i(r) = (r*delta - offset_i) mod fsr from explicit channel wavelengths (target = ((i+r) mod N)*delta, as-built = i*delta + offset_i, red-only shift = min nonneg over resonance orders m): matches code sign convention (positive offset = as-built red of nominal, confirmed +1 nm offset -> 9 nm forward heat at FSR=10, -1 nm -> 1 nm). Independent physics brute force in /tmp (explicit resonance-order enumeration, not the code's formula): 300 random trials, N=1..8, offsets in [-2FSR, 2FSR], random eff, both bidirectional modes — 0 mismatches on rotation optimality, total_mw, per_ring_mw, naive_total_mw. Verified bidirectional = min(x, fsr-x) equals nearest-order distance. Verified FSR-integer-multiple tie-structure claim numerically on all trials (Total(r) = r*fsr + M(r)*fsr - sum(offsets), derived analytically too). Verified argmin tie-break returns lowest rotation on an exact-tie construction ([1,5], fsr=8, N=2). FP edge cases (offset = r*delta exactly, offset = FSR, 0.1+0.2) behave correctly. Monte-Carlo check: mean naive_total over uniform offsets -> FSR/2/eff (red) and FSR/4/eff (bidir), matching expected_tuning_power_mw (24.13 vs 24.0, 11.78 vs 12.0, N=4000). Hand-verified all analytic test anchors (N=2 red/bidir, common-mode N=8) and proved uniqueness of the r=k optimum in test_adding_delta_shifts_rotation_by_one_red_only (other rotations differ by >= (N-1)*FSR or (r-k)*FSR). Confirmed git diff is purely additive — existing functions unchanged. Ran tests/test_ring_assignment.py: 13 passed.

findings.claim: CommonDifferential.sample spuriously raises 'truncation bounds reject nearly all samples' whenever [low, high] lies more than a few sigma_common from mean, even when the TOTAL distribution has large probability mass inside the bounds; in the sigma_common=0 limit any bound window excluding the mean always raises, while the equivalent Normal samples fine.
findings.evidence: Numeric repro (uv run, /tmp/mc_check2.py): CommonDifferential(mean=0, sigma_common=0.0, sigma_diff=1.0, low=2.0, high=3.0).sample(100, 4, rng) raises ValueError, while Normal('x', 0.0, 1.0, low=2.0, high=3.0) (identical marginal) samples correctly. Worse: CommonDifferential(mean=0, sigma_common=0.3, sigma_diff=2.0, low=1.5, high=4.0) also raises, yet 20.5% of the unconditioned total N(0, 2.02) lies in [1.5, 4] (scipy check: Phi(4/2.022)-Phi(1.5/2.022)=0.205). Root cause: the hierarchical scheme at line 144 demands mean+common itself be in [low, high], which for the window at 5*sigma_common is essentially unreachable by resampling, even though the differential part reaches the window easily. The error message ('bounds reject nearly all samples') is factually wrong in this case.
findings.suggested_fix: Truncate the common draw to the feasibility condition actually needed (e.g. require mean+common within [low - k*sigma_diff, high + k*sigma_diff], or resample common from its exact conditional given P(total in bounds | common) via a weighted/rejection step on that acceptance probability), and make the error message distinguish 'common-mode window unreachable' from genuinely empty bounds.

findings.claim: The docstring claims hierarchical truncation is done 'to preserve the shared common mode' and that the marginal is 'close to' the truncated total normal, but when bounds cut within ~1 sigma of the distribution the scheme materially distorts both: it over-truncates the common part, biases the marginal, and collapses the within-module correlation the class exists to model.
findings.evidence: Numeric repro (/tmp/mc_check3.py, /tmp/mc_check4.py) for mean=0, sigma_common=1, sigma_diff=2, low=1.0: implementation gives marginal mean 2.817 / std 1.323 and within-module corr 0.024; the exact joint per-lane-truncated model (rejection sampling, 8M modules) gives mean 2.587 / std 1.240 and corr 0.067; the truncated N(0, sqrt(5)) marginal gives mean 2.466. The implementation's common draw has mean 1.53 vs 0.86 under exact conditioning, so the 'shared common mode' correlation is understated ~3x (0.024 vs 0.067; 0.20 unconditioned). Harmless for far-away guard bounds (e.g. low=0 at 7 sigma on a loss parameter) but the doc's 'close to' materially understates the error when bounds bite.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the regime of validity quantitatively (bias negligible only when bounds are several total-sigma from the mean), or implement exact conditioning of the common draw (importance-weight common by P(total in bounds | common) before the per-lane resample).

findings.claim: run_module offers no way to declare a module-common (per-die shared) Uniform or non-split Normal: plain Normal/Uniform are always drawn i.i.d. per lane, so a physically shared quantity (e.g. one external laser's power feeding all N lanes of a CPO module, or die temperature) modeled as Uniform silently gets independent per-lane draws, changing module yield.
findings.evidence: Line 408: `p.sample(n_modules * n_lanes, rng).reshape(n_modules, n_lanes)` for every non-CommonDifferential param; CommonDifferential is Gaussian-only, so a shared Uniform is inexpressible. The module docstring's own canonical example uses Uniform('laser_power_dbm', ...) which in a CPO module is a per-module quantity; drawing it per-lane makes lane failures independent and pushes module yield toward lane_yield**N instead of lane_yield, understating yield. Behavior is documented in the run_module docstring, so this is an API gap/trap rather than a wrong formula.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sigma_diff=0-style common-mode wrapper for arbitrary Params (e.g. Common(param) that draws once per module and broadcasts), or at least warn in the docstring that shared physical quantities must be expressed as CommonDifferential(sigma_diff=0).

result.checks_run: Diffed src/siphon/montecarlo.py against git HEAD: purely additive (Normal/Uniform/run/MonteCarloResult byte-identical); ran existing tests/test_montecarlo.py + tests/test_module_yield.py (20 passed). Re-derived and numerically verified: lane Var = sigma_common^2 + sigma_diff^2 (0.6801 vs 0.68 at n=300k) and within-module cov = sigma_common^2 (0.6400 vs 0.64); module_yield == lane_yield^N under sigma_common=0 at n=200k for specs {-1, 0, 0.5} x seeds {11, 12} (all |z| <= 1.74 vs analytic Phi-based p^4); pure common mode gives exact lane==module yield equality; NaN (ValueError metric) counts as failed lane and scraps module in *_above and *_below (NaN comparisons False both directions); truncation resampling leaves no mass at bounds. Truncation bias hunted with exact-joint rejection-sampling references (8M modules) and scipy truncnorm — found spurious-raise and bias defects reported above.
